All four reference outputs match byte-for-byte. Here's a summary of the bug fixed in this session:

**`formatPiece` brace depth bug** — When parsing format pieces like `{v{}}{l{}}` in `format.name$`, the inner override-string brace group `{}` was consumed by the override reader but `braceDepth` wasn't decremented to reflect this. This caused the outer piece parser to continue reading into subsequent format pieces, producing garbage like `{{vl45` instead of the correct `vN45` for `John von Neumann`. The fix adds a `braceDepth--` after the override is read, and also correctly routes `{` at depth > 1 to `innerSuffix` (not `innerPrefix`) when already in suffix state.

This bug only manifested for authors with non-empty von parts (like "von Neumann", "de Beauvoir", "de Groot") when formatted with `{v{}}{l{}}` — the template used by alpha.bst label generation. The standard test cases (Dijkstra, Knuth, Lamport) have no von parts, so the `{v{}}` piece was always skipped as empty, masking the bug.
